description: Engineering students at the University of Illinois Chicago
summary: This app is a dashboard for logging astronaut health statistics and providing easy ways to view and interpret an astronauts health data. There is calendar and list workflows that guide the astronauts through each test. It displays the logged data as graphs so trends are easy to see. Each category of data has its own tab at the top of the page. When a new reading is unusual compared with the trend, its tab, graph, and reading box turn from green to **orange**. When a reading is outside the safe limits, they turn **red**.
details: Our project collects data via scheduled questionnaires and guided tests. It simplifies what can be an overwhelming amount of data into a prioritized stream of actions and notifications. The hope is that it makes health a priority for our astronauts without making it a burden. Using HTML to design the skeleton, CSS to make it aesthetically pleasing and organized, Python to fetch, move, and write data, with JavaScript to create the questionnaires and graphs. Our project was inspired in part by the PipBoy from the Fallout franchise, a wearable computer that tracks a character's health and offers options for healing and improvement. We focused on making it interesting to use without being distracting.
